$schema-note: COR-B W1 (audit AC2-2). The single source for substrate ownership: which service owns each table and each public function. Read by tests/integration/platform/ownership-manifest-conformance.test.ts (completeness) and tests/integration/platform/internal-api-conformance.test.ts (the inner-ring direction rule, ADR-U047 rule 3). Adding a table without classifying it here fails the suite red. Ground truth: ADR-U023 (DS/PC decomposition), ADR-U047 (+A1, A2), ADR-U048 + ruling R-1 (notifications), rulings R-2 (consent = PC-2) and R-3 (content_families = DS-3).

content_families.note: Ruling R-3 (2026-07-19): DS-3 for now; moves to DS-4 when Content is built.

ds5_config.note: FEAT-PD015 (N-C): DS-5 operational settings as data, mirroring pc2_config (which is likewise owned by its prefix's service). RLS-enabled with no policies — deny-all to clients, read only by SECURITY DEFINER paths. First key is the platform-wide-announcement nudge policy; DS-5 because the routing layer above the delivery substrate is DS-5's (see the notifications note), not the vertical's.

notifications.note: ADR-U048 + ruling R-1: the Notifications-vertical delivery substrate. Written by every tier as obligation-fulfilment, NEVER a boundary crossing (ADR-U047 rule 5). Deliberately not a DS table — the inner-ring gate must not treat writes to it as crossings. DS-5 takes the routing/preferences layer above it when built.

notification_categories.note: FEAT-PD013 (N-A): the V3 §6 category catalog (lawful basis + interruption grade). Relabelled vertical:notifications → DS-5 at COR-C W4 (Audit III ruling R-4, 2026-07-31): these rows are precisely the routing inputs ds5_may_deliver reads, and ADR-U048 clause 2 assigns routing metadata to DS-5. The DS-5 label puts the table in dsTables(), so a non-DS-5 reach-in now fails the inner-ring gate — under the vertical label it sat ungated. The notifications.type FK pointing here is delivery-substrate → routing-registry, data-level and one-way; the function-body gate is unaffected by FKs.

notification_kinds.note: FEAT-PD013 (N-A): the notification-event kinds registry (kind → category). Relabelled vertical:notifications → DS-5 at COR-C W4 (Audit III ruling R-4, 2026-07-31) — same rationale as notification_categories. The pinned vertical-set test in ownership-manifest-conformance.test.ts states the boundary.

notification_channels.note: FEAT-PD016 (N-D): the open registry of delivery channels (in_app delivering, email stored-but-not-delivering). Classified DS-5 rather than vertical:notifications — unlike the kind/category catalogs, which describe WHAT the platform may say and are FK'd by the delivery table, this describes HOW the routing layer delivers, which is DS-5's half of the ADR-U002 boundary (the ds5_config rationale). Ruling R-4 (COR-C W4, 2026-07-31) settled the family this note used to flag: all three routing registries (channels, categories, kinds) are DS-5; only the delivery table itself stays vertical:notifications.

notification_preferences.note: FEAT-PD016 (N-D): per-member x per-category x per-channel preferences; absence of a row means allowed. DS-5 per the 2026-07-26 preference-home adjudication (board row ND-1), which ruled out Platform Core because the category_key FK would have pointed Core → Domain (docs/platform/CLAUDE.md:38). Deliberately classified DS-5 rather than vertical:notifications so the table lands in dsTables() and IS policed by the internal-API conformance gate: the whole point of ND-1 was keeping Core out of this substrate, so a future Core function reaching in must fail a test rather than pass unseen. Consent is unmoved (PC-2 substrate / PC-4 contract, ADR-U034).

export.note: COR-C W2 (Audit III AC3-4, closing GC-5): the Art. 15/20 completeness classification. Every table above must appear here — export-completeness-invariant.test.ts fails red on an unclassified table, so a new member-data table cannot ship without an export decision. memberData:true entries name their representation in the get_own_data_export() document (or a cited exemption); memberData:false entries state why no member rows exist. Column-level completeness stays the composing contract's concern; this gate is table-level.

pc2_config.reason: platform operational config; no member rows

reaper_runs.reason: system reaper run log; aggregate counts, no member attribution

groups.representation: profile.display_name (the personal group IS the member's display identity) + memberships[].group_name (contextual)

group_roles.reason: per-group role definitions; communal config, not member rows

user_group_roles.representation: roles section (inline core; added at COR-C W2 — the invariant's first catch: roles held were member data with no export path)

exemption.reason: transient invitation state: invitee e-mail addresses are third-party data under the own-data wall (the C-E precedent that omits reports' target_group_id); the caller-attributable act resolves into group_memberships on acceptance, which is exported
exemption.citation: C-E board own-data wall (20260721100000:495-501) + COR-C W2 review 2026-07-31

exemption.reason: operational/security log; the member-facing right-of-access shape for audit trails (own actions vs actions about the member by third-party actors) is an A-ADM design question — deferred to the A-ADM area-open design session, alongside TASK-OBS-01's sink decisions
exemption.citation: COR-C W2 review 2026-07-31; revisit at A-ADM area open

exemption.citation: COR-C W2 review 2026-07-31; ADR-U026 (studios own authoring)

journey_enrollments.representation: journeys section (get_own_step_instances_export — enrollment context: status + timestamps)

conversations.representation: communication.conversation_participations (conversation metadata via the caller's participation rows)

announcements.representation: communication.authored_announcements (own-authored rows; added at COR-C W2 per Stefan's AC3-16 ruling, 2026-07-31)

content_reports.representation: communication.reports_submitted (own reports; target identity omitted per the own-data wall)

ds5_config.reason: DS-5 operational settings; no member rows

notification_preferences.representation: notification_preferences section (get_own_notification_preferences_export; composed at COR-C W2 — AC3-3, the section the audit found orphaned)

lifecyclePrefixNote: ADR-U047 rule 1: the ds{N}_lifecycle_ prefix is reserved for domain-owned lifecycle-fact handlers. Auto-allowed by prefix — the owning service is read from the digit, so these need no explicit entry above.

verticalComposition.citation: ADR-U047 Amendment 2 (2026-07-19), audit AC-4, COR-A W8, PR #191; composes restructured at COR-C W2 (Audit III AC3-15 — the prose list had gone two contracts stale and nothing noticed). Whole-account export completeness (GDPR Art. 15/20): composes the contracts below platform-side so one RPC returns the complete document on every surface. Read-only, contract-only — calls the domain's published READ contracts, never their tables. The composes array is LOAD-BEARING: export-completeness-invariant.test.ts asserts the live body calls exactly this set (GC-6).

exceptions.crossServiceReadsNote: COR-B W2: a DS-N function referencing a DS-M table (M != N) must appear here AND be downward (M < N), per the anatomy's acyclic dependency rule — DS-1 at the bottom, DS-7 at the top, nothing depends on DS-7. Empty today: audit II found no live DS-to-DS reference.
